2027 Mazda3 Goes Live, US Model Gets One Manual Trim Level
14 photos
Photo: Mazda
The row-your-own crowd has had a pretty rough 2026 thus far. Volkswagen discontinued the manual from the Jetta GLI for good, while Honda is temporarily pausing Civic Si production. Over at Mazda, the manual is alive and well in the 3. There is, however, a big catch regarding the configuration.
For starters, the 2027 Mazda3 cannot be had with three pedals unless you go for the hatchback. Secondly, front-wheel drive is a must. And thirdly, prospective customers must spend $31,950 from the outset. Said price does not include destination charge, which adds $1,315 to the final price.
The 2.5 S Premium Plus 6MT with front-wheel drive slots between the 2.5 S Preferred AWD, which is $29,990 at launch, and the 2.5 S Premium Plus. The latter comes in at $33,350 before destination and options, while the range-topping 2.5 Turbo Premium Plus will set you back a cool $38,190 for the hatchback or $37,040 for the sedan.
A bit of an oddity as of this writing, the sole manual 3 available for model year 2027 does not belong to the sporty compact club. That makes the manual grade all the more interesting, especially when you remember that increasingly more automakers prefer two-pedal setups due to improved fuel economy and better acceleration figures.
Under the hood, its 2.5-liter naturally aspirated I4 makes a respectable 186 horsepower on 87-octane regular unleaded. The Premium Plus grade makes the manual-equipped hatchback a sweet daily, for it comes with LEDs fore and aft, 10.25-inch touchscreen infotainment, a heated steering wheel, the Active Driving Display, and adaptive front lighting that swivels through corners for improved visibility on winding roads.
Photo: Mazda All other grades, be they hatchback or sedan, feature a six-speed automatic that does not like to be hurried. The sedan with said tranny in 2.5 S flavor is $24,750 for model year 2027, making it a compelling buy. Even so, there are cheaper alternatives, including the 22,390-dollar K4 from Kia. Speaking of, the much fresher design from Kia boasts segment-leading rear seat legroom for 2027.
Going for the manual-equipped Mazda3 isn't something one does with their head. Putting our sensible pants on, the Preferred hatchback is a much better pick when it comes to value for money. Starting at $28,040 in the US, the Preferred brings eight-way power adjustments and memory for the driver's seat, heating for both front seats, a power moonroof, wireless charging, and a passenger-side mirror that automatically tilts down when reversing.
All-wheel drive further complicates things, with Mazda offering the Preferred hatchback with all-wheel drive from $29,990 (or $31,305 after destination). Prospective customers of the 2.5 Turbo Premium Plus with all-wheel drive get up to 250 horsepower and 320 pound-feet (434 Newton-meters) at full chatter, albeit only with 93-octane premium dino juice.
Filling it up with 87 octane drops both numbers, with Mazda claiming 227 hp and 310 lb-ft (420 Nm). Presumably due to the manual's inherent limitations, the force-fed engine is not compatible with said manual. The rest of the 2027 model year changes are concentrated on everyday equipment.
Cordless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are now standard from the Select Sport up, which further sweetens the deal with Alexa built-in, 18-inch black alloys, dual-zone climate control, leatherette upholstery, and rain-sensing wipers. Preferred adds Qi wireless phone charging and extra comfort goodies.
